title: Insert Interval: Adding a Road Closure
summary: Copy the closures that end before the new one, absorb the ones it overlaps, then copy the rest.

analogy.scenario: A road crew's schedule closes a lane on days 1–2, 5–7, and 9–12, sorted and never overlapping. A new closure for days 6–10 must be added, combining any it touches.

mapping.abstract: An interval in the sorted list

takeaway.summary: In one pass: copy intervals that end before the new one starts, absorb those that start at or before its end (growing it), place it, and copy the rest.
whenToUse: Adding a range to a sorted, non-overlapping list
Updating a schedule with one new booking

scenes.narration: A road crew has lane closures planned for days 1 to 2, 5 to 7, and 9 to 12. A new closure is needed for days 6 to 10. What does the combined schedule look like?
scenes.caption: Closures on days 1–2, 5–7, 9–12; a new one for days 6–10

scenes.narration: You could add the new closure, sort everything again, and merge from scratch. But the list is already sorted, so one pass does it: copy, absorb, then copy the rest.
scenes.caption: Re-sorting and re-merging the whole list is more work than needed

scenes.narration: The first closure ends on day 2, before the new one starts on day 6. It can't touch it, so it's copied unchanged.
scenes.caption: Days 1–2 end before day 6: copy them as they are

scenes.narration: Days 5 to 7 start on day 5, before the new closure ends on day 10. They overlap, so absorb them: the new closure now starts on day 5.
scenes.caption: Days 5–7 start before day 10 ends: absorb, now 5–10

scenes.narration: Days 9 to 12 start on day 9, still before day 10. Absorb them too: the closure now runs from day 5 to day 12.
scenes.caption: Days 9–12 start before day 10: absorb, now 5–12

scenes.narration: Nothing is left to absorb, so place the grown closure. The schedule is days 1 to 2, then 5 to 12.
scenes.caption: Place days 5–12: the schedule is 1–2 and 5–12

scenes.narration: Closures are intervals and the new one is newInterval. Copy what ends before it, absorb what starts by its end, then copy the rest. One pass, O(n) time.
scenes.caption: Copy before, absorb overlaps, copy after: O(n)
